problem_type: CI external binary downloads lack persistent cache ownership
symptom: Multiple Linux and macOS jobs failed installing Electron 43.4.1 with HTTP 504 after merges #1457 and #1463. The rerun still failed packaging macOS and compiling the installer guard because builder toolset downloads returned HTTP 504.
direct_cause: setup-node caches the pnpm store but not Electron ZIPs downloaded by postinstall. Electron-builder also downloads NSIS and packaging toolsets outside the pnpm store.
class_root: No shared pre-install boundary restores external binary caches or prevents new jobs omitting them.
affected_population: All CI dependency-install jobs on Linux, macOS and Windows
Eight packaging jobs, release validation gates and the Unit job (three full-mode shards) that compile installers
entry_points: 24 pnpm install job definitions (22 run scripts; two use --ignore-scripts)
10 builder-consuming job definitions: 8 packaging, 1 release validation and 1 Unit matrix (12 full-mode executions)

external_sources.purpose: Check cache override and default directories.
Check pinned downloader options; no added installer retry.
Check primary keys, prefix restore and successful-job save.
Version browser caches and retain uncached OS dependency installation.
Confirm ELECTRON_BUILDER_CACHE and all platform defaults; cross-check installed app-builder-lib 26.15.3 getCacheDirectory.

invariants: Every dependency/browser install restores the shared cache first.
The actual downloader environment and cached paths agree.
Keys use runner OS, architecture and the resolved lockfile version; restore prefixes stay on the same OS and architecture.
Installation and checksum/identity validation always run, including cache hits.
Every builder packaging or installer test job enables the shared builder cache before execution; the cache key separates workflow/job toolset populations.
generality_proof: The same action sets job-wide cache paths on all platforms and all 24 install jobs. All six browser installers inherit the Playwright path. The all-workflow structural test rejects omitted, late or conditional cache steps and conflicting environment declarations. The JS door-map covers ensureElectronRuntime only; the YAML/shell entry census is enforced by the structural test. All builder entry jobs are derived from workflow commands and package.json script aliases, including full/focused Unit tests. Their whole matrix inherits the builder cache. Workflow/job-specific primary keys prevent a partial target cache permanently claiming every target; same-platform prefixes still seed missing jobs. Release validation also enables builder caching because run-gates-tests can select the installer compile tests.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own job-wide external binary paths and versioned actions/cache restoration before installation.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both restore the shared action first; unit also installs Chromium through the existing shell script.
Same action and lower-case electron_config_cache are exported through GITHUB_ENV for Windows.
Still restores the action, so future postinstall enabling cannot silently omit the binary cache.
Both enable the same builder cache. Unit full-mode shards 1,2,3 and focused mode inherit it before any test selection.

recurrence.reason: An external outage reaches multiple operating systems and each future ephemeral runner.
same_class_scan: git grep -n "pnpm install" -- .github: 24 run commands in 11 workflows, excluding one comment.
git grep -nE "playwright install|ci-install-chromium|curl|wget|download|postinstall" -- .github: six Chromium installs; release/artifact downloads occur after installation.
package.json pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies permits electron, esbuild and platform ffmpeg/ffprobe packages; registry-packaged platform binaries stay in the pnpm store.
git grep electron-builder, dist:mac:dir, test:unit:shard and test:system:focused in all workflows; trace package.json scripts plus scripts/packaging/installer-compile.cases.mjs build() calls.

prevention.invariant: All CI external binary consumers restore versioned cache before install and share exact downloader paths.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing lockfile version fails preparation; missing or mismatched wiring fails Contracts. Cold-cache upstream failures remain visible.
prevention.strategy: One composite action owns paths and restore keys; an all-workflow node test in Contracts detects omissions without per-job allowlists. Register the shared owner and the scanning test; split node:test from Vitest in the pre-push batches without exemptions.

legacy_paths.rationale: No alternate installer exists; existing install and identity validation remain the only runtime path.

dependency_lifecycle.target: Retain pinned versions while their cache APIs and checksums satisfy the action contract.
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: This is missing CI cache ownership, not a dependency-version defect; version changes are outside the task.
exit_criteria: When Electron changes installer/cache variable semantics, inspect the lockfile-selected installer and pass the path/key contract before updating this action.
When Playwright changes browser version or cache layout, prove the new lockfile key and effective PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH on a real runner.
When electron-builder changes toolset cache layout, re-check ELECTRON_BUILDER_CACHE propagation and the real NSIS/package workflows before updating cache schema.

migration: No user data migration; initial runner caches are cold and save only after successful jobs.
residual_risks: First cache seed and GitHub cache availability still depend on external infrastructure.
Actual CI save, subsequent cache hit and absence of Electron Releases download remain unverified until coordinator push/rerun.
